clue.text: Most gorgeous nuisance, drunk coming in

indicators.note: the drunk is said to come into the nuisance, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: a pest is a nuisance
a lush is a habitual drunk

explanation.surface: A troublesome drunk barges into some glamorous gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Plush means luxurious and sumptuous, so the superlative is the most gorgeous.

clue.text: Worthless talk from fine fellow coming into fortune

explanation.definitionFit: Piffle is nonsense, a synonym for idle, worthless chatter.

clue.text: As king once was falsely supposed to be, mostly ignorant

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word is kept, its final letter dropped

explanation.surface: A historical aside about a king's undeserved reputation for being mostly ignorant.
explanation.walkthrough: Ethelred's Old English nickname meant 'poorly counselled', so calling him unprepared is the false supposition; 'mostly' cuts the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not having read about a subject is uninformed, hence ignorant of it.

clue.text: A lot of drink may get one rooting in the ground possibly

explanation.surface: Heavy drinking might leave someone grubbing about on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words to see the pig's head that roots in the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large barrel measure, so it holds a great quantity of beer or wine.

clue.text: Dynasty's anthem?
